subtopics.title: The Longitudinal Profile — A River Seen From the Side

questions.question: A longitudinal profile is best defined as:
options: A side view of a river along its full length, from source to mouth
A cross-section drawn from bank to bank
A map of the whole drainage basin
A graph of the river's discharge through the year

questions.question: A graded profile is identified by:
options: A waterfall in the upper course
A smooth, concave curve with no steps or ponded flats, erosion and deposition in balance
A level stretch behind a reservoir wall
A convex bulge in the middle course

questions.question: The permanent base level of a river is:
options: The deepest pool in its channel
The floor of its largest reservoir
Sea level — the level of the water body it drains into, below which it cannot erode
The band of hardest rock it crosses

questions.question: The valley cross-sections at the two ends of a profile differ in that:
options: Both ends show the same narrow V-shape
The mouth end is a deep gorge and the source end a floodplain
Neither end shows any recognisable shape
The source end is a deep narrow V from downward cutting, while the mouth end is wide and flat-floored from sideways swinging

subtopics.title: How a Meander Works — Two Banks, Two Jobs

questions.question: Meanders typically develop:
options: In the upper course where vertical erosion dominates
Only where the rock is uniformly hard
At waterfalls and rapids
In the lower course, on gentle gradients, where lateral erosion dominates

questions.question: The outer bank of a meander bend is steep because:
options: The fast outer current undercuts and collapses it
Sediment piles up against it
The rock there is always harder
Vegetation binds it into a wall

questions.question: The paired names for the inner bank of a meander are:
options: River cliff and undercut slope
Slip-off slope and point bar
Watershed and interfluve
Levee and terrace

questions.question: Over many floods, a meander loop:
options: Stays fixed in one position
Straightens itself out completely
Enlarges and migrates across the valley floor, widening the floodplain
Moves upstream towards the source

questions.question: The neck of a meander narrows because:
options: Deposition builds it inward from both sides
The river dries up seasonally
Vegetation compresses the soil
Outer-bank erosion on both limbs of the loop eats into it from both directions

questions.question: The river finally abandons the loop when:
options: A major flood breaks through the thinned neck and the shorter, steeper breach becomes the main channel
The loop freezes over in winter
The inner bank collapses into the channel
The loop erodes down to bedrock

questions.question: The cut-off loop is separated from the new channel by:
options: A wall of bedrock exposed by the flood
Deposition of sediment sealing the loop's two ends
A dam built across the breach
Tree roots blocking the junctions

questions.question: In old age, an oxbow lake becomes:
options: A new tributary of the river
A waterfall
A silted, reed-filled meander scar — a curved marshy depression on the floodplain
A delta at the river mouth

subtopics.title: Reading Profiles and Meanders in the Exam

questions.question: On a longitudinal profile sketch, a vertical step with resistant rock hatched beneath it represents:
options: A waterfall
The permanent base level
An oxbow lake
A floodplain

questions.question: On a photograph of a meander, the fast side of the channel is located by finding:
options: The widest stretch of water
The gentle sandy bar sloping into the water
The line of trees on the floodplain
The steep, raw, collapsing bank — the undercut slope

questions.question: On a topographic map, an oxbow lake appears as:
options: A straight blue canal beside the river
A detached crescent of blue or marsh symbols lying beside a looping river
A circle of crowded contours
A triangular symbol with a station number

questions.question: Looping bends locked inside a deep gorge with contours crowded on both banks are:
options: Braided channels
Distributaries on a delta
Incised meanders — old loops cut vertically downward by a rejuvenated river
Meander scars

subtopics.title: The Slide From the Mountain to the Sea

questions.question: In the slide picture, the perfect one-swoop slide stands for:
options: The graded profile — smooth, concave, steep at the source and flat at the mouth
The drainage basin
A river in flood
The cross-section of a gorge

questions.question: The jolting ledge and the stalling pan on the unfinished slide represent:
options: Two tributaries joining the river
A waterfall over resistant rock and a reservoir ponding the flow
The source and the mouth
An oxbow lake and its scar

questions.question: The splash pool at the bottom of the slide — the level the river can never dig below — is:
options: The temporary base level
The watershed
The floodplain
The sea, the permanent base level

questions.question: A deep narrow V-shaped valley on a profile sketch signals:
options: The lower course, where the river swings sideways
A graded stretch of the profile
The upper course, where the young river cuts straight down
An area of deposition

questions.question: In the taxi picture, the passenger pressed against the far window represents:
options: The slow inner current that deposits sand
The fast outer current that erodes the bank
The river's source
The flood that breaks the neck

questions.question: The gentle beach of sand on the inside of a bend exists because:
options: The inner water moves slowly and cannot keep hold of its load, so it deposits
The wind blows sand into the river there
The outer bank supplies it directly
The rock on the inside is softer

questions.question: The wide flat floodplain beside an old river is the work of:
options: A single catastrophic flood
Wind erosion over centuries
Glaciers that once filled the valley
Meander loops migrating across the valley floor and sweeping it level

subtopics.title: The Shortcut Through the Empty Plot

questions.question: The diagonal schoolyard path stands for:
options: The old meander loop
The river's breakthrough channel across the neck — shorter, steeper and quicker
The floodplain
The watershed between two basins

questions.question: The two teams tunnelling towards each other represent:
options: Deposition on the two inner banks
Two tributaries joining the main stream
Outer-bank erosion attacking the neck from both sides
Reeds closing in on the lake

questions.question: The gates of sand in the story are:
options: The deposits that seal the two ends of the abandoned loop
The walls of the gorge
The levees along the main channel
The dunes beside the estuary

questions.question: The correct order of the eight-step oxbow story is:
options: Flood breakthrough, neck narrows, erosion begins, lake forms
Outer banks eroded, inner banks built, neck thinned, flood breakthrough, shortcut adopted, ends sealed, oxbow lake, meander scar
Ends sealed, shortcut adopted, neck thinned, lake forms
Meander scar, oxbow lake, flood, erosion
